page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the n4 family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical Intel x86_64 cores with hyper-threading enabled, resulting in 2 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 32 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4 GB of RAM per vCPU. The underlying Intel processor includes an L3 cache of 260 MB, alongside an L2 cache of 2 MB and an L1d cache of 48 KB. It supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix multiplication and vector operations, alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations place the n4-standard-8 in the average performance tier for most compute and memory tasks. The single-core and multi-core Geekbench scores are 1770 and 6838 respectively, while the Passmark CPU score is 11489.89, indicating stable mid-range processing capabilities. Memory read bandwidth reaches up to 530.44 GB/sec for small cached blocks, though it drops to 61.33 GB/sec for larger uncached blocks, reflecting a standard memory architecture. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (36.22 GB/sec) and Passmark memory scores (1809.35) are relatively weak, falling into the bottom 25% of tested hardware. However, the instance demonstrates solid performance in static web serving throughput at 12.95 GB/sec and handles small-scale LLM inference adequately, processing 642.95 tokens/sec for prompt processing on a 135M parameter model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n4-standard-8 offers a balanced resource profile that avoids the premium pricing of memory-optimized or specialized GPU instances. It is designed for workloads requiring consistent, dedicated CPU performance without extreme memory or storage demands. Suitable workloads include general-purpose web serving, software compilation, database operations, and moderate text or image processing tasks. It can also support lightweight machine learning inference for small models, though its weak multi-threaded decompression and large-block memory write performance (37.65 GB/sec) make it less suitable for heavy data-shuffling or memory-intensive ETL pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-8 is an x86_64 general-purpose instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical Intel cores and 32 GB of RAM. It includes advanced CPU features like Intel AMX and AVX-512, supported by a 260 MB L3 cache. Lacking local storage and GPUs, it relies on network-attached storage. Performance benchmarks place this instance in the average tier, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 6838 and static web serving throughput of 12.95 GB/sec. While memory bandwidth for small cached blocks is strong at 530.44 GB/sec, large-block memory operations and multi-threaded decompression show weaker performance. Qualitatively, the n4-standard-8 provides a balanced, cost-efficient resource profile for general-purpose applications. It is best suited for web serving, software compilation, database operations, and lightweight machine learning inference.
